name: IRS2005STRPBF
title: IRS2005: 200 V high and low side gate driver, in 8-lead SOIC and MLPQ 4x4
summary: The IRS2005 drives two N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs: one low-side output referred to COM and one floating high-side output whose return can sit up to 200 V above it, supplied by a bootstrap. Each output follows its own logic input, which takes 3.3 V, 5 V or 15 V logic. It sources 290 mA and sinks 600 mA typ, with 160 ns and 150 ns typical delays matched within 50 ns, and both supplies have undervoltage lockout. Named uses are appliance motor drives, servo drives, micro inverters and three-phase inverters. IRS2005STRPBF is the SOIC on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: One IRS2005 drives a pair of N-channel MOSFETs on a bridge rail of up to 200 V. VCC feeds the chip and, through a diode, the bootstrap capacitor between VB and VS, which powers the high-side output. A capacitor decouples VCC to COM. HO and LO each reach a gate through a series resistor. The high-side source joins VS and one load terminal; the low-side drain goes to the other load terminal and its source to ground with COM. A capacitor holds the high-voltage rail to ground.
notes: Pin numbers follow the lead assignment of the package in use.

operation.text: Two output channels with their own references: LO works from VCC against COM, and HO works from the floating VB-VS supply, so it can switch a high-side N-channel MOSFET or IGBT whose source rides up to 200 V. The floating supply is meant to come from a bootstrap diode and capacitor. Gate supplies run up to 20 V per channel; VS may swing negative in transients, and its slew is rated to 50 V/ns.

HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, each output high while its input is high; the two channels are independent. The inputs accept CMOS or LSTTL levels down to 3.3 V logic: a high is at least 2.5 V and a low at most 0.8 V. A high input draws up to 10 µA at 5 V.

Both VCC and the floating VBS supply have an undervoltage detector. Each turns on at 8.0 V to 9.8 V (8.9 V typ) and turns off at 7.4 V to 9 V (8.2 V typ), a hysteresis of 0.7 V typ. The VCC threshold is referred to COM and the VBS threshold to VS.

HIN enters through a Schmitt-trigger input with a pull-down resistor, is gated with the VCC undervoltage detector and drives a pulse generator. Its output crosses to the floating well through a high-voltage level shifter, then a pulse filter, into the set and reset inputs of an RS latch; the VBS undervoltage detector drives a second reset input. The latch drives the HO output pair. LIN enters through the same kind of input, is gated with the VCC undervoltage detector and reaches the LO output pair through a buffer. The minimum pulse input filter time is 300 ns typ.
The logic keeps working with VS from -8 V up to 200 V. When VS sits between -8 V and -VBS, the logic state is held.

The outputs are high pulse-current buffers with low cross-conduction inside the driver. At 15 V bias each sources at least 200 mA (290 mA typ) into a shorted output and sinks at least 420 mA (600 mA typ), for pulses up to 10 µs. Into 1000 pF the rise time is 70 ns typ and the fall time 30 ns typ.

Turn-on delay ton runs from the input's 50 % point to the output reaching 10 %, and rise time tr from 10 % to 90 % of the output. Turn-off delay toff runs from the input's 50 % point to the output falling to 90 %, and fall time tf from 90 % to 10 %. Delay matching MT is how far the high-side and low-side delays differ for the same edge; it is at most 50 ns.

The SOIC is marked S2005, the MLPQ S2005M, with a date code (year and work week), a lot code carrying a four-digit code, and an assembly site code. A 'P' in the marking code position shows a released lead-free part.
